criteria.evidence: Article opens with a direct yes-with-limits answer to 'is muay thai good for self-defense' and holds the honest-evaluation POV from the brief throughout: real strengths (clinch, elbows/knees, composure) named without oversell, then limits (no ground game, no disarms, no de-escalation) named without hedging. Zero DTV/service angle, matching the explicit top-funnel positioning of the command.

Every H2/H3 opens with its conclusion before detail: e.g. 'The real strengths are narrower than most gyms admit' (real-strengths), 'Here's what most gyms won't say out loud... muay thai has real gaps' (honest-limits), 'No single art covers everything' (how-it-compares). FAQ answers lead with yes/no/depends before elaborating. The two new sourced sentences (clinch, Krav Maga) sit mid-paragraph as supporting detail, they do not displace the BLUF opener of their section.

First-person Meaw voice grounded early ('I'm Meaw. I run Wildcat Muay Thai in Chiang Mai'), opinion asides kept ('it's the part I care about most', 'I'd argue it's the most useful one'). The two inline citations use the project's established attribution pattern ('according to [Source name](url)', same construction as dtv-visa-cost-breakdown.md), no dry academic tone introduced. No warrior/beast-mode register, no invented stats, ages, prices or competitor claims. Zero em dash (checked: review-static em_dash.* all PASS at 0).

All spec keywords still reformulated naturally in prose: 'is muay thai good for self-defense', 'is muay thai dangerous', 'good for a real street fight', 'how muay thai compares to boxing', 'good exercise', 'muay thai training' (single bold, no duplicate). The two new sentences read as natural prose extensions, not inserted citation dumps.
